newsitem.title: GERMANY: Resilient German DAX edges up to set new records.
newsitem.headline: Resilient German DAX edges up to set new records.

text.p: German shares turned higher after a slow start on Thursday, with the DAX led up by the futures market to fresh record highs and coming tantalisingly close to the magical 3,000-point level.
Dealers, who have been aiming for days to push the DAX over the key 3,000 threshold, said the rally was not over yet.
"The champagne bottles will be out," said a Frankfurt trader. "There is more in this market. The uptrend is definitely still there."

The DAX closed the bourse session up 4.86 points at a record closing high of 2,993.31, having earlier hit a record intra-day high of 2,998.61 and having risen over 20 points from an early low of 2,970.45.
The market was weakened at the start after an overnight drop on Wall Street but proved resilient enough to track the futures market into positive territory.

March DTB DAX futures, which have been volatile ahead of an options expiry deadline tomorrow, galavanised the cash market into action by vaulting the 3,000 point level. They were trading up 21 points at 3,011 as bourse trading ended.
Dealers noted a sharp shift in sector preferences, with bank shares now firmly in demand, replacing the clear favourites of recent weeks -- chemical stocks.
Deutsche Bank rose 1.67 marks at 78.47 marks, while Dresdner Bank rose 65 pfennigs to 51.15.
Dealers said bank shares had not kept up with chemical stocks' recent rally and were now starting to make up lost ground.
At the same time, BASF AG slipped 99 pfennigs to 59.60 marks while Hoechst AG was down 87 pfennigs at 69.58 marks.
Utility RWE jumped to as high as 70 marks before settling back at 68.80 marks, up 40 pfennigs, after news that it was to receive partial damages for delays in operating a nuclear power plant.
For the DAX as a whole, the 3,000 point level has no technical significance, but is rather seen as a key psycological boost for the market.
"It will certainly look better on paper," was one trader's comment. "But it will not mean a brand new era."
